reference: Independent host hexdump CLI (the util-linux hexdump implementation, which is the counterpart documented by the published implementation documentation). This is not GNU coreutils; results are byte comparisons against that external implementation. Bash type/help behavior is checked separately against the documented loadable metadata contract.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
Canonical output for control, printable, high-bit, and short-row bytes
Default little-endian word output and an odd trailing byte
Hexadecimal skip and octal byte-limit arguments
Skip and limit across concatenated input files
Repeated redirected stdin in one persistent shell
Unknown-option error status and diagnostic presence
Zero counts across default, shortcut, custom and skip modes; empty inputs; missing arguments; invalid counts; repeated dash operands.
exclusions: No real device, host path, network input, or unbounded stream is opened.
The custom-format tests cover documented common format units, not the full util-linux color/file format language.
Device-backed input remains deferred pending a disposable VM or reviewed bounded mock.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata reports the registered loadable as a builtin, and help resolves its documented builtin entry.
cases.script:
PATH=
[[ $(type -t hexdump) == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help hexdump)
[[ $help_text == *hexdump* ]]
printf 'builtin\n'

cases.purpose: Canonical mode formats control bytes, printable ASCII, DEL, high-bit bytes, and a final row shorter than 16 bytes.
The no-option default renders little-endian 16-bit words and a one-byte final word, then reports the final offset.
-s accepts a hexadecimal offset and -n accepts an octal byte limit; output offsets retain the skipped-byte position.
Checks the reference behavior for a zero-byte canonical limit, including whether a final-offset line is emitted when no bytes are consumed.
Skip and limit apply to a small concatenated logical input spanning two relative fixture files.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > left.bin
printf 'DEFGHI' > right.bin
hexdump -C -s 2 -n 5 left.bin right.bin

cases.purpose: A documented one-byte custom format prints each byte as two lowercase hexadecimal digits, including NUL and high-bit values.
Three fresh stdin redirections in the same Bash process each produce a complete canonical dump.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\000Z' > stdin.bin
hexdump -C < stdin.bin
hexdump -C < stdin.bin
hexdump -C < stdin.bin

cases.purpose: Identical full rows fold to an asterisk in normal mode, while -v prints every duplicate row; a short final row follows both runs.
cases.script:
printf 'abcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnopQ' > repeated.bin
hexdump -C repeated.bin
hexdump -C -v repeated.bin

cases.purpose: An unsupported option is rejected with the reference command's status and a diagnostic rather than producing a dump.
Exercise bounded reads and errors when the input is a device-backed special file.
cases.reason: Character-device cases (r1 to r3) are only missing fixtures, using VM-local sandbox nodes. A device read error (r5) uses SECCOMP-NOTIFY. Only block-device input (r4) needs a driver-provisioned loop device: the guest's /dev/vda is root:disk 0660 and loop attach needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

cases.purpose: Zero count in default, shortcut, custom, and skip-plus-canonical formats.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > input
hexdump -n 0 input
hexdump -x -n 0 input
hexdump -e '1/1 "%02x\n"' -n 0 input
hexdump -C -s 2 -n 0 input

cases.purpose: Missing required option arguments and invalid count values retain reference failure status.
cases.script:
for opt in -n -s -e; do
 rc=0
 hexdump "$opt" || rc=$?
 printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
done
for arg in bad -1 ''; do
 rc=0
 hexdump -n "$arg" || rc=$?
 printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
done

cases.purpose: Repeated dash operands share stdin once per invocation; each fresh redirection reads the complete stream. Expected bytes follow the documented logical-stream extension.
cases.script:
printf 'A' > input
hexdump -C - - < input
hexdump -C - - < input

cases.purpose: Compare empty input and an offset reaching EOF against independent hexdump in default, canonical, and shortcut modes.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'abc' > input
hexdump empty
hexdump -C empty
hexdump -x empty
hexdump -C -s 3 input
